title: Archive a Run with Exceptions
subtitle: Retain the block and the loaner
scenario: Sam started on a loaner. Archive the run honestly: retain it, and flag that it carried exceptions (the backorder and loaner). An archive that hides the mess cannot teach the loop anything.
input: Onboarding for hire H-4022 is complete - the hire started on a loaner while the ordered laptop ships. Archive under run id onboarding-H-4022 with 7-year retention. Flag exceptionsNoted = true (backorder + loaner) and seedsCatalog = true.
instructions: Record the hire id and the archived run id.
Flag exceptionsNoted true (the run had a block) and seedsCatalog true.
Return one valid JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build one JSON archive record: hireId H-4022, archivedRun onboarding-H-4022, retention 7 years, exceptionsNoted true (backorder + loaner), seedsCatalog true.
successMessage: Run archived with its exceptions. The mess is retained so the loop can learn from it.
editorHelper: Retain the run - and flag that it carried exceptions.

intro.heading: Archive the truth, not a highlight reel

sections.title: Exceptions are the lesson
sections.body: A clean run teaches little. This run's backorder and loaner are exactly what the loop should learn from - so the archive flags them instead of smoothing them over.

sections.title: Retention still governs
sections.body: The 7-year retention applies to messy runs too. The exception flag makes the interesting runs findable when someone asks 'how often does hardware slip?'.

sections.title: Feeds a better catalog
sections.body: seedsCatalog true means this run's lessons flow to profile-feedback. A repeated backorder is a signal the policy or a loaner pool should change.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: An archive record that retains the run and flags its exceptions for the loop.

fieldGuide.meaning: The hire whose run is archived.

fieldGuide.hint: It seeds the catalog, so true.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd file the run with a note about the backorder and loaner, so the pattern is visible next time.

tools.powerAutomate: write the run with an exceptions flag and retention label
tools.zapier: archive the record and tag it as having exceptions
tools.python: store the run with exceptionsNoted for later analysis

takeaway.heading: Run archived with exceptions
points: You retained a messy run honestly, exceptions flagged.
The exception flag makes the interesting runs findable.
seedsCatalog true sends the lesson to the feedback loop.
A repeated backorder is now a signal the catalog can act on.
The workflow can now retain and learn from runs that did not go clean.
